[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Data Cleaning and Imputation Strategies in Data Science"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Real-world data is inherently messy, often containing missing values, duplicates, format inconsistencies, and outliers. Data cleaning and imputation are foundational steps in the data science pipeline that ensure model accuracy and reliability."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Understanding Missing Data Mechanisms"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Before applying any imputation strategy, it is critical to understand why data is missing. Statisticians generally classify missing data into three categories:"},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Missing Completely at Random (MCAR): The probability of data being missing is independent of both observed and unobserved data."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Missing at Random (MAR): The probability of missingness depends systematically on observed data, but not on the missing data itself."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Missing Not at Random (MNAR): The missingness is directly related to the unobserved values themselves."},{"order":8,"type":"subheading","text":"Basic Imputation Techniques"},{"order":9,"type":"paragraph","text":"For numerical datasets, simple imputation replaces missing values with statistical measures derived from the column itself, such as the mean, median, or a constant value."},{"order":10,"type":"code","text":"import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from sklearn.impute import SimpleImputer

# Sample DataFrame with missing values
data = {'Age': [25, np.nan, 30, 45, 22],
        'Salary': [50000, 60000, np.nan, 80000, 45000]}
df = pd.DataFrame(data)

# Applying Mean Imputation
imputer = SimpleImputer(strategy='mean')
df['Age'] = imputer.fit_transform(df[['Age']])"},{"order":11,"type":"subheading","text":"Advanced Imputation with KNN"},{"order":12,"type":"paragraph","text":"When features exhibit strong correlations, K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) imputation provides a more sophisticated approach. It estimates missing values based on the similarity of other data points."},{"order":13,"type":"code","text":"from sklearn.impute import KNNImputer

# Initialize KNN Imputer with 2 neighbors
knn_imputer = KNNImputer(n_neighbors=2)
df_imputed = pd.DataFrame(knn_imputer.fit_transform(df), columns=df.columns)
print(df_imputed)"},{"order":14,"type":"subheading","text":"Best Practices for Production Pipelines"},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Always split your data into training and testing sets before calculating imputation parameters like mean or median to prevent data leakage."},{"order":16,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Combine imputation with machine learning pipelines using scikit-learn's Pipeline class for reproducibility."},{"order":17,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Monitor the proportion of missing data. If a feature has more than 60 percent missing values, consider dropping the feature entirely unless it holds high domain significance."}]
